answer: Every identity must keep a lantern slice of the attestation log: the epoch beacon and its own key assign it a unique set of record chunks to store and serve on demand. Auditors fire chunk requests at unpredictable, comet-timed moments; a missed or slow reply is a public signal that flags the identity. Because beacon-derived slices are disjoint, 1,000 fakes cannot pool one disk — each owes the full slice every epoch, while an honest agent stores one small slice and answers a handful of requests.
